filename: A simple emulator that enables interpretation of parameter-output relationships, applied to two climate model PPEs.pdf
title: A simple emulator that enables interpretation of parameter-output relationships, applied to two climate model PPEs
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
testbed_rationale: Publicly releases PPE parameter-to-metric tabular data and emulation codes for both GISS ModelE3 and CESM2 CAM6, providing an accessible benchmark for sparse climate model emulation and sensitivity analysis.
pain_points: Extreme sparsity: high parameter dimensionality (43-45 parameters) with very limited sample sizes (200-800 ensemble members).
Emulating aggregated skill score metrics rather than raw outputs flattens or obscures nonlinear parameter responses.
Outliers in small PPEs degrade emulator stability and performance.
Emulating all outputs jointly in neural networks can degrade performance on variables driven by independent parameter mechanisms.
extraction_notes: The manuscript was submitted to JAMES and posted as an arXiv preprint in October 2024. The study develops 'sage', an interpretable, additive GP-based emulator with fixed hyperparameters to avoid overfitting in sparse parameter spaces.
